chunks: Yaqub ibn Akhtab narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered the Kaaba only once, and he spread his garment beneath his feet and removed his sandals.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Kaaba, the cubic structure in Mecca built by Abraham and Islamized by Muhammad, the holiest site in Islam.
key_terms.بَسَطَ: He spread out or laid flat.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet enter the Kaaba and what was his etiquette inside?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s singular entry into the Kaaba, emphasizing his physical humility by spreading his garment and removing his shoes, which establishes a key etiquette (adab) for worshippers. In Shia jurisprudence, this act is often cited to support the recommendation of removing footwear when entering the Kaaba, distinguishing it from the general practice in the rest of the mosque. The event underscores the Kaaba not merely as a structure but as a purified space deserving of specific reverence.
